- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

113	func TestCacheConcurrency(t *testing.T) {
114		ctx := context.Background()
115		cache := NewDefault()
116		defer cache.Close()
117	
118		const goroutines = 10
119		const operationsPerGoroutine = 100
120	
121		var wg sync.WaitGroup
122		wg.Add(goroutines)
123	
124		for i := 0; i < goroutines; i++ {
125			go func(id int) {
126				defer wg.Done()
127	
128				baseKey := fmt.Sprintf("worker%d-", id)
129	
130				// Set operations
131				for j := 0; j < operationsPerGoroutine; j++ {
132					key := fmt.Sprintf("%skey%d", baseKey, j)
133					value := fmt.Sprintf("value%d-%d", id, j)
134					cache.Set(ctx, key, value)
135				}
136	
137				// Get operations
138				for j := 0; j < operationsPerGoroutine; j++ {
139					key := fmt.Sprintf("%skey%d", baseKey, j)
140					val, ok := cache.Get(ctx, key)
141					if !ok {
142						t.Errorf("Key '%s' should exist in cache", key)
143						continue
144					}
145					expected := fmt.Sprintf("value%d-%d", id, j)
146					if val != expected {
147						t.Errorf("For key '%s', expected '%s', got '%s'", key, expected, val)
148					}
149				}
150	
151				// Delete half the keys
152				for j := 0; j < operationsPerGoroutine/2; j++ {
153					key := fmt.Sprintf("%skey%d", baseKey, j)
154					cache.Delete(ctx, key)
155				}
156			}(i)
157		}
158	
159		wg.Wait()
160	
161		// Verify size and deletion
162		var totalKeysExpected int64 = goroutines * operationsPerGoroutine / 2
163		if cache.Size() != totalKeysExpected {
164			t.Errorf("Expected cache size to be %d, got %d", totalKeysExpected, cache.Size())
165		}
166	}

171		evictedMu := sync.Mutex{}

175		config.CleanupInterval = 25 * time.Millisecond
176		config.OnEviction = func(key string, value interface{}) {
177			evictedMu.Lock()
178			evicted[key] = value

194		evictedMu.Lock()

## Summary of Redis Connection Configuration and Cache Layer Setup

Based on my thorough search of the repository, I found **NO Redis integration**. Instead, the project uses an **in-memory cache layer** built from scratch. Here are my findings:

### Cache Architecture

**Location:** `/bench/repo/store/cache/` directory

**Main Files:**
1. **`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`** - Core in-memory cache implementation
2. **`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache_test.go`** - Comprehensive cache tests
3. **`/bench/repo/store/store.go`** - Store initialization with cache setup
4. **`/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go`** - User settings cache usage
5. **`/bench/repo/store/user.go`** - User cache usage
6. **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/instance_stats.go`** - Instance stats cache
7. **`/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`** - RSS feed cache

### Cache Configuration (TTL & Settings)

**Default Configuration** (`/bench/repo/store/store.go`, lines 40-45):
```go
cacheConfig := cache.Config{
    DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}
```

**Cache Config Interface** (`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`, lines 41-54):
- `DefaultTTL`: Default time-to-live for all cache entries (10 minutes default)
- `CleanupInterval`: How often cleanup runs (5 minutes default)
- `MaxItems`: Maximum number of items in cache (1000 default)
- `OnEviction`: Optional callback when items are evicted

### Cache Instances in Store

Three separate cache instances initialized in `/bench/repo/store/store.go` (lines 27-29):

1. **`instanceSettingCache`** - Cache for instance settings
2. **`userCache`** - Cache for users
3. **`userSettingCache`** - Cache for user settings

### User Cache TTL Details

**User Entry TTL:** Uses default 10-minute TTL
- **Cache Key Format:** `userCacheKey(userID int32)` returns `strconv.Itoa(int(userID))`
- **Location:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go`, line 88-90

**User Setting Entry TTL:** Uses default 10-minute TTL
- **Cache Key Format:** `getUserSettingCacheKey(userID, key)` returns `fmt.Sprintf("%d-%s", userID, key)`
- **Location:** `/bench/repo/store/cache.go`, lines 7-9
- **Affected Settings:** Shortcuts, General, Tags, Refresh Tokens, Personal Access Tokens, Webhooks

### Instance Stats Cache TTL

**Specific Short TTL** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/instance_stats.go`, line 21):
```go
const instanceStatsCacheTTL = 60 * time.Second
```
This is a specialized single-value cache for admin-only instance statistics, refreshed every 60 seconds.

### RSS Feed Cache TTL

**RSS Cache Settings** (`/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`, lines 23-27):
```go
const (
    maxRSSItemCount      = 100
    defaultCacheDuration = 1 * time.Hour      // 1 hour TTL for RSS feeds
    maxCacheSize         = 50                  // Max 50 cached feeds
)
```

### Cache Features

- **Thread-safe:** Uses `sync.Map` for concurrent access without locks
- **TTL Expiration:** Automatic cleanup loop based on `CleanupInterval`
- **Memory Management:** Implements LRU eviction when `MaxItems` limit is exceeded
- **Size Estimation:** Tracks approximate memory footprint of cached items
- **Eviction Callbacks:** Optional `OnEviction` handler for cleanup operations

### Connection Pools & Configuration

**No Redis or external cache connections exist.** All caching is in-process memory using Go's `sync.Map` for thread-safe operations.

**Cleanup Goroutine:** Each cache instance spawns a background goroutine that periodically:
- Removes expired entries based on TTL
- Evicts oldest items when max capacity is exceeded
- Invokes optional callbacks for cleanup logic

The system is designed for single-server deployments with embedded in-memory caching, not distributed caching via Redis.
